evidence: Found 2026-08-19 while adding a test suite. Both paths are tracked in git as mode 120000 symlinks whose target is the ABSOLUTE local path /home/l3thal/brain/10-swingby/swingby/web/<app>/node_modules. git ls-tree HEAD web/pre-launch/ -> '120000 blob 640a5e8b... web/pre-launch/node_modules'. Consequences: (a) any clone on another machine gets a dangling symlink where node_modules should be; (b) a git worktree gets a symlink pointing back into the PRIMARY tree, so two checkouts silently share one dependency tree — an npm install in one mutates the other; (c) node_modules should never be tracked at all. fix_hint: git rm --cached the two symlink entries, add node_modules/ to .gitignore, and let npm create the real directory. If the symlink existed to save disk, use npm workspaces or a shared store (pnpm) rather than a path committed into the repo.

evidence: Found 2026-08-19 when a unique index on push_tokens.token FAILED to apply against production: 'Key (token)=(ExponentPushToken[Qglc...]) is duplicated'. Live query: that one token has 4 rows and 4 DISTINCT user_ids, first_seen 2026-07-31, last_seen 2026-08-18. Mechanism: register_push_token upserts with on_conflict='user_id,token', which dedupes per (user, token) PAIR — so the same physical device accumulates one row per account that has ever logged in on it. A physical device has exactly one current owner, so the invariant should be one row per TOKEN. The unregister endpoint's own docstring states the risk plainly ('Called on logout. Without it, the token row survives sign-out and the next user to log in on the same physical device would receive the previous user's notifications') — it is mitigation that depends on logout firing, and it did not fire here 3 times out of 4.
fix_hint: Dedupe keeping the most recent row per token, add the unique index, and change the upsert to on_conflict='token'. Logout-based cleanup stays as defence in depth, but must not be the only thing preventing the leak.
notes: 2026-08-20: Dedupe + unique index APPLIED to production and verified (0 duplicates, index present); endpoint now upserts on_conflict=token.
repro: select token, count(*), count(distinct user_id) from push_tokens group by token having count(*)>1;  -- returns 1 token, 4 rows, 4 users
title: One Expo push token is registered to 4 different users — notifications leak across accounts on a shared device
verify: select count(*) from (select token from push_tokens group by token having count(*)>1) d;  -- must be 0. AND a unique index on push_tokens(token) must exist. AND register_push_token must upsert on_conflict='token' so re-registering REASSIGNS the device rather than adding a row.

evidence: Requested by the owner 2026-08-20 ('when someone posts we need to include the area code — postal code or just NW/SE/NE'). Root cause found in privacy.py: mask_address_to_locality keeps everything AFTER the first comma, and in Canadian addressing the quadrant sits BEFORE it. So '3823 16 St SW, Calgary, AB' masks to 'Calgary, AB' and the quadrant — the one piece of geography a business uses to judge the drive — is exactly what gets thrown away. Every post in the feed looked identical. Measured against the 77 live posts: 70 (90%) state a quadrant in the address; the 7 that do not are 2 nulls, a city-only 'Calgary, AB', two incomplete free-typed strings, and two posts that are not in Calgary at all (Orillia ON and Saint-Albert QC). Postal codes are NOT an option: zero of 77 addresses contain one.
fix_hint: Derive the quadrant from the address TEXT before truncation and emit it as its own 'area' field. Do NOT compute it from lat/lng: checked against 12 live posts, the Centre Street/Centre Avenue cross disagreed with the stated quadrant twice (200 Barclay Parade SW computes NW; 823 Radford Rd NE computes SE) because Calgary's boundaries follow the Bow River and downtown convention. A wrong quadrant sends a tradesperson across the city.
notes: 2026-08-20: Quadrant derived from the address text and emitted as 'area'; rendered on JobOpportunityCard. 25 area tests, backend 1396 passed, 106 mobile component tests. Coordinate-based derivation deliberately rejected — 2 wrong in 12 against live data.
repro: Browse the business job feed — every card reads 'Calgary, AB' regardless of where the job is.
title: Job feed shows only 'Calgary, AB' — masking discards the quadrant, so every post looks equally far away
verify: cd backend && pytest -q tests/test_area.py  — 25 tests. Then check a masked row: mask_service_post_row({'address':'3823 16 St SW, Calgary, AB'}) must return area='SW' AND address='Calgary, AB' with the street gone.

evidence:
[WRONG ALGORITHM] `useAuthDeepLink` (mobile/App.js:65) is mounted unconditionally in `RootNavigator`, running whether or not `user` is already set — but `completeAuthFromUrl`'s own header comment claims "A confirmation link arrives precisely when the user is logged OUT" and the code never checks that. If a logged-in user (or anyone testing multiple accounts on one device) opens any old/foreign `swingby://auth-callback#access_token=...` link, `storeSession()` at line 134 unconditionally overwrites the SAME `swingby_token`/`swingby_refresh_token` SecureStore keys the currently active session uses (see TOKEN_KEY/REFRESH_KEY in services/auth.js), and `setAuthToken()` swaps the axios client onto the new (possibly bad) token — before the new token is validated.

Proof: if the subsequent `getMe()` at line 138 then fails, the catch block at 140-149 deletes BOTH SecureStore keys entirely and sets `setAuthToken(null)`, permanently destroying the previously-valid session's persisted tokens. The in-memory React `user` state (owned by AuthContext, untouched here since `adoptSession` is never called on this path) still shows the old user as logged in, so nothing looks wrong until the next app restart or access-token expiry, at which point the real session can no longer be restored or refreshed and the user is silently logged out with no explanation.

notes: 2026-08-21: Triage 2026-08-20 — NOT A BUG on main; re-verified at f22818d. The finding reports the ABSENCE of the 50/50 confirm/complete split as a blocker. On main that absence is deliberate and documented: settle_on_date_confirmed() and settle_on_complete() were DELETED (see the comment block now occupying budget_settlement.py:138-158) precisely because they were correct, tested, unreachable code that read like a specification and did not match the app's behaviour. evidence:
[WRONG ALGORITHM] `LiveStatusActions` (rendered on `JobManagementScreen`'s Status tab) drives a provider through en_route → arrived → started → completed purely via `POST /bookings/{id}/events`. Its own confirm dialog says "This may release final payment" and its terminal state says "Job marked complete. The client has been notified," but `create_event` in `booking_events.py` only inserts a `booking_events` row and sends a push — it never touches `bookings.status` or calls the escrow release path. The module's own docstring even claims otherwise ("On 'completed' we also call the existing payment-release path used by PATCH /bookings/{id}/complete") in the same paragraph that admits the opposite ("we just emit the event here"). The real completion path exists one component away on the same tab: `StatusTracker` (`JobManagementScreen.js:479`) calls `handleAdvance('completed')`, which does `PATCH /bookings/{id}/complete` (`JobManagementScreen.js:239-240`) — the only thing that actually flips status and releases money.

Proof: `LiveStatusActions.js:71-82` `postEvent` body is only `api.post(\`/bookings/${bookingId}/events\`, { event_type })`; `:114-121` renders "Job marked complete. evidence:
[WRONG NUMBERS] `GET /businesses/me/analytics`'s `total_earnings` and `GET /analytics/export`'s `total_revenue` both gate a booking's released earnings on `escrow.is_capture_backed(p)` after already filtering to `status == "fully_released"`. `is_capture_backed()` explicitly returns `False` for any row not in `CAPTURED_ON_PLATFORM = ("paid_full", "held", "partial", "partial_released")` — a tuple that deliberately excludes `"fully_released"`, by its own docstring, because "nothing is HELD once escrow is released." That means every genuinely Stripe-captured, on-platform, completed booking (the normal case) is misclassified as unverified, and `total_earnings`/`total_revenue` can only ever be nonzero for off-platform (cash/e-transfer) payments. `payments.py` hit this exact inversion and was fixed on 2026-08-03 by switching to `escrow.was_ever_captured()` (which still exists specifically for this), but the identical fix was never ported to `businesses.py` or `analytics_export.py`.

Proof: `escrow.py:75` `CAPTURED_ON_PLATFORM = ("paid_full", "held", "partial", "partial_released")` — no `"fully_released"`. `escrow.py:222-224` `if payment.get("status") not in CAPTURED_ON_PLATFORM: return False` / `return bool(payment.get("stripe_payment_intent_id"))` — for a `fully_released` on-platform row this always returns `False` before ever checking the PaymentIntent. `escrow.py:227-244`'s own docstring for `was_ever_captured`: "`is_capture_backed` ... deliberately excludes `fully_released` ... WRONG for every historical reader." `payments.py:123-133` — the 2026-08-03 (D5) fix comment states verbatim: "Every legitimately completed and released booking is 'fully_released', so the 'verified' figure was **always zero**... the exact inversion of what this field is for," then switches to `was_ever_captured`. `businesses.py:403-411` still does `if p.get("status") != "fully_released": continue` then `if escrow.is_capture_backed(p): total_earnings_c += cents else: unverified_earnings_c += cents` — same unfixed pattern. `analytics_export.py:230,265-269` — same: `verified = escrow.is_capture_backed(p)`, then `total_revenue_c = sum(r["_released_c"] for r in rows if r["status"] == "fully_released" and r["verified"])`. `backend/tests/test_analytics_export.py:166-176`'s own fixture comment admits the masking: every test asserting a nonzero `total_revenue` uses `"method": "cash"` (off-platform, which short-circuits `is_capture_backed` before the status check) — no test ever exercises a real on-platform Stripe-captured `fully_released` row.
